summary: PJM's MC Legal Report lists FERC orders and PJM filings from September 14 to October 16, 2026. It records the dismissal of rehearing of the EL26-67 show cause order, the ER26-3515 Large Load Registry order and the ER26-3380 backstop order.

points.point: PJM reports FERC dismissed rehearing and clarification requests on the show cause order as premature, with the proceeding in abeyance through November 16, 2026.
points.quote: FERC concluded that the Show Cause Order is not a final agency action, because it made only preliminary findings and initiated further proceedings

points.point: The report notes FERC will give no clarification while the abeyance lets PJM's stakeholder process and section 205 filings proceed.
points.quote: FERC also declined to provide clarification while this proceeding remains in abeyance through November 16, 2026

points.point: On October 9 FERC accepted part of PJM's Large Load definition and registry filing and set a November 8 compliance date for the rest.
points.quote: The Commission directed PJM to submit a compliance filing by November 8, 2026, of the tariff sections with the Large Load definition and the Large Load Registry

points.point: On September 29 FERC accepted the Reliability Backstop Procurement revisions effective February 28, 2027, and opened EL26-108 on cost allocation, exit responsibility and collateral.
points.quote: the Commission accepted PJM’s proposed Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP) Tariff revisions, subject to refund and further proceedings and effective February 28, 2027.

points.point: PJM asked on October 12 to hold the EL26-108 paper hearing in abeyance pending its forthcoming section 205 filing.
points.quote: requesting to hold the paper hearing proceedings, and any additional briefings, in abeyance pending resolution of PJM’s forthcoming Section 205 filing

points.point: DOE emergency orders under FPA section 202(c) let PJM direct backup generation at large loads to run before or during an EEA 3.
points.quote: authorizing PJM to direct backup generation resources at large loads to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (“EEA”) 3 or during an EEA 3

throughLine.text: Summarizes PJM-side developments around the E-7 show cause order: the September 21 rehearing dismissal, the Large Load Registry order, the backstop order and DOE emergency orders touching large loads.
